annotations.title: Suggest a price from the frontier price model

description: Ask the frontier price model what it would charge for one of your products: it reads your own quotes for that product from the last 90 days (rebased onto today's price) and where the offer sits, and returns the price, the chance of a sale there and at today's price, the margin per quote when you give unit_cost, and the acceptance curve. It looks at most 10% past prices you have already quoted, inside min_price and max_price. A suggestion only: nothing is quoted, stored or learned, and no other workspace's quotes are read. Without unit_cost it maximises revenue. Answers not_released while it is not switched on for your workspace. Needs a Last Price credential with routing read scope.

category.description: A category id; its top-level ancestor is the vertical.

channel.description: Where it is sold, such as the web, an API, MCP or a marketplace.

current_price.description: Today's price. Defaults to the price of the product's latest quote.

product_id.description: The product, as your pricing calls name it.

topology.description: How it is priced: posted, metered, per-call, seat, subscription, outcome, auction, negotiated, marketplace, bundle or dynamic.

unit.description: What one unit is: item, call, token, seat-month, month, hour, gb, outcome or percent.

unit_cost.description: What one unit costs you. Without it the suggestion maximises revenue.

name: suggest_frontier_price
